topic.title: What happens inside your car's engine in the second you turn the key: the starter motor

shape.name: The chain reaction
shape.beats: hook: the action you do (turn the key) and the hidden part it wakes -> each part pushes the next, one push a beat (switch, solenoid, pinion, ring gear, pistons) -> payoff: the code's figure that explains why the small part can move the big one -> the release (what stops it breaking) -> where it came from, one line -> back to the action (loop)
shape.why: a machine_works topic told as a row of parts physically pushing each other, the owner's 'understand it by seeing it'; reveal is already 2 of the last 9

demand.title: EVER WONDERED HOW A START MOTOR WORKS?

title: How Can a Motor This Small Start a Whole Engine?
description:
How can a motor that fits in your hand start a whole car engine?
We cut a starter open in 3D and watch the solenoid, the pinion, the ring gear and the one-way clutch do their jobs, one push at a time.
Sources: Saab WIS service manual, IEEE Engineering and Technology History Wiki (Jan 1995).
Animations are simplified illustrations, not exact to scale.
subject: The car starter motor
